items.front: Sangam Age dates and meaning of 'Sangam'?
items.back: c. 300 BCE – 300 CE; 'Sangam' = assembly of Tamil poets/scholars under royal (Pandya) patronage.
1st Madurai (Agastya, none survive); 2nd Kapadapuram (Tolkappiyar → Tolkappiyam); 3rd Madurai (Nakkirar → Ettuthokai+Pattuppattu).

items.front: Muvendar — emblem · capital · port for each?
items.back: Chera: bow · Vanji (Karur) · Muziris. Chola: tiger · Uraiyur · Puhar. Pandya: fish · Madurai · Korkai.

items.front: Karikala Chola — key battle and monument?
items.back: Won the Battle of Venni; built the Kallanai Dam (Grand Anicut) on the Cauvery — among the world's oldest dams still in use.

items.front: Elara — who was he and how did he die?
items.back: Early Chola king who ruled Sri Lanka justly (praised in Mahavamsa); defeated & killed by Sinhalese prince Dutugemunu.

items.front: Cheran Senguttuvan — what is he famous for?
items.back: Founded the Pattini Cult (Kannagi); Himalayan expedition; contemporary of Gajabahu — the 'Gajabahu synchronism' dates the Sangam Age.
items.examPoint: Cheran Senguttuvan — Pattini cult & Gajabahu synchronism

items.front: Which Chera king led a Himalayan expedition, recorded in which work?
items.back: Imayavaramban Nedum Cheralathan; recorded in Pathitrupathu. (Udhiyan Cheralathan fed both Mahabharata armies.)
items.examPoint: Imayavaramban Nedum Cheralathan — Himalayan expedition & Pathitrupathu

items.front: Pandya king who won Thalaiyalanganam; who ordered Kovalan's execution?
items.back: Thalaiyalanganaattu Neduncheliyan won that battle; Aryappadai Kadantha Neduncheliyan ordered Kovalan's execution (→ Kannagi burnt Madurai).

items.front: Earliest Tamil grammar; the Eight & Ten collections?
items.back: Tolkappiyam (by Tolkappiyar); Ettuthokai = Eight Anthologies; Pattuppattu = Ten Idylls.
Thiruvalluvar; 1,330 couplets; Aram (Virtue), Porul (Wealth), Inbam (Love). Part of the Pathinenkilkanakku.

items.front: The twin epics of Tamil — titles & authors?
items.back: Silappathikaram (Ilango Adigal, Kannagi–Kovalan) & Manimekalai (Sittalai Sattanar, a Buddhist epic — their daughter).

items.front: The five tinai (landscapes) and their nature?
items.back: Kurinji (hills), Mullai (pastoral), Marudam (farmland), Neydal (coast), Palai (desert). From the Tolkappiyam.

items.front: Sangam revenue terms: Karai, Ulgu, Irai, Iravu?
items.back: Karai = land tax; Ulgu = customs duty; Irai = tribute from chiefs; Iravu = extra/forced demand.
items.examPoint: Revenue system — Karai, Ulgu, Irai, Iravu

items.front: Proof of Indo-Roman trade in Tamilakam; main port for Rome?
items.back: Hoards of Roman gold/silver coins across Tamil Nadu; Muziris (Chera) was the chief Roman-trade port. Exports: pepper, pearls, textiles.

items.front: Which invasion ended the Sangam Age; which site gives it material proof?
items.back: The Kalabhra invasion (~3rd c. CE, the 'dark age'). Keeladi (Keezhadi) on the Vaigai proves a literate, urban Sangam society (Tamil-Brahmi).
items.source: ASI / TN Archaeology; APPSC GK — Sangam Age
